# MayFly Full Documentation LLM Reference

## About MayFly
MayFly is a zero-external-dependency local secrets manager written in 100% pure Go standard library. It encrypts developer API keys and environment variables at rest using AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption and RFC 8018 PBKDF2 key derivation (600,000 iterations), and injects them directly into child application volatile memory (RAM) at runtime via native host OS execution primitives (`os/exec`).

## Quick CLI Reference
- `mf init`: Initializes encrypted vault bound to the current folder's hardware inode.
- `mf set KEY=VALUE`: Encrypts a key-value secret directly into `~/.mayfly/vault.enc`.
- `mf get KEY`: Decrypts and prints a secret value.
- `mf list`: Lists all configured secret keys in current project.
- `mf delete KEY`: Removes a secret key.
- `mf <command>`: Decrypts secrets into RAM and executes the target process (e.g., `mf npm run dev`, `mf python main.py`, `mf go run .`).
- `mf scan`: Scans the current repository for unencrypted `.env` files or hardcoded API keys.
- `mf audit verify`: Validates cryptographic SHA-256 integrity of the local access log.
- `mf`: Launches the full-screen interactive 2D double-buffered terminal user interface (TUI).

## Zero-Dependency Architecture
MayFly replaces 12 common external dependencies (including godotenv, pbkdf2, bubbletea, fatih/color, atotto/clipboard, trufflehog) with standard library implementations in Go stdlib.
